Adverse Effects Sodium hydroxide is strongly alkaline and corrosive, and rapidly destroys organic tissues. The ingestion of caustic alkalis causes immediate burning pain in the mouth, throat, substernal region, and epigastrium, and the lin- ing membranes become swollen and detached. There is dys- phagia, hypersalivation, vomiting with the vomitus becoming blood-stained, diarrhoea, and shock. In severe cases, abdominal pain, asphyxia due to oedema of the glottis, circulatory failure, oesophageal or gastric perforation, peritonitis, or pneumonia may occur. Stricture of the oesophagus can develop weeks or months later. Caustic alkalis on contact with the skin can produce full thick- ness burns leading to extensive damage. Alkali burns to the eyes cause conjunctival oedema and corneal destruction; damage may be irreversible. Treatment of Adverse Effects Ingestion should not be treated by lavage or emesis.
